# The ScMaSigPro object

## Two resolutions and the results

An analysis works at two resolutions: the cells, with their pseudotime and
path, and the pseudotime bins whose pseudo-bulk counts the models are fitted
to. A `ScMaSigPro` object holds both as `SingleCellExperiment` objects, one
per slot, because their columns differ: `altExp()` needs the columns of the
main experiment, and bins kept in `metadata()` would lose the checks and the
accessors of an experiment. The other slots hold the results of the steps,
which have no place in a `SingleCellExperiment`, and a record of every
setting. Every step returns the object with one more slot filled, and checks
it with `validObject()`.

```{r slots-table, echo = FALSE}
code <- function(x) paste0("`", x, "`")
slots <- data.frame(
    Slot = code(c(
        "Sparse", "Dense", "Design", "Profile", "Estimate", "Significant",
        "Parameters", "version"
    )),
    Class = code(c(
        "SingleCellExperiment", "SingleCellExperiment", "MatrixDesign",
        "VariableProfiles", "Estimates", "Significant", "ParameterConfig",
        "character"
    )),
    `Filled by` = c(
        "`as_scmp()`, `create_scmp()`", "`sc.squeeze()`, `sc.restruct()`",
        "`sc.set.poly()`", "`sc.p.vector()`", "`sc.t.fit()`",
        "`sc.filter()`, `sc.cluster.trend()`", "every step",
        "the creation of the object"
    ),
    `Read with` = c(
        "`cSparse()`, `eSparse()`", "`cDense()`, `eDense()`",
        "`predictors()`, `pathAssign()`, `showPoly()`", "`scmpResults()`",
        paste(
            "`showSol()`, `showCoeff()`, `showGroupCoeff()`, `showTS()`,",
            "`showInflu()`, `showSigProf()`"
        ),
        "`scmpResults()`", "`showParams()`", "`updateObject()`"
    ),
    check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(slots)
```

The bundled object `scmp.ob` holds the analysis of the
[Quick start](https://spriyansh.github.io/scMaSigPro/articles/scMaSigPro.html)
vignette; printing it summarises every step that has run:

```{r scmp-ob, message = FALSE}
library(scMaSigPro)
data("scmp.ob", package = "scMaSigPro")
scmp.ob
```

## Cells and bins

`cSparse()` and `cDense()` return the metadata of the cells and of the bins
as data frames, and `eSparse()` and `eDense()` their counts, by default the
`counts` and `bulk.counts` assays. Each has a replacement form
(`cSparse<-` and so on) that checks the new value and the object.

```{r cells-bins}
head(cSparse(scmp.ob)[, c("Pseudotime", "Path", "scmp_binned_pseudotime")], 3)
bins <- cDense(scmp.ob)
head(bins[, c("Path", "scmp_binned_pseudotime", "scmp_bin_size")], 3)
eSparse(scmp.ob)[1:3, 1:4]
eDense(scmp.ob)[1:3, 1:4]
```

The names of the columns are kept in the parameters (`ptime_col`,
`path_col`, `bin_col` and others), which `showParams()` lists.

## The design

`predictors()` returns the design of the model, one row per bin and one
column per term besides the intercept; `pathAssign()` the binned pseudotime
and the path of each bin; `showPoly()` the model as a formula.

```{r design}
showPoly(scmp.ob)
head(predictors(scmp.ob), 3)
head(pathAssign(scmp.ob), 3)
```

## The results

`scmpResults()` gathers the results of every gene in one table: the test of
the full model, the selected model, the gene lists and the cluster.
`scmpToRowData()` writes the same columns into the `rowData()` of a
`SingleCellExperiment`. The `show*()` readers return the parts of the
selected models: `showSol()` their p-values and R-squared, `showCoeff()`
their coefficients, `showGroupCoeff()` the coefficients of the polynomial of
each path, `showTS()` the t statistics, `showInflu()` the bins with
influential observations and `showSigProf()` the pseudo-bulk counts of the
genes with a selected model.

```{r results}
head(scmpResults(scmp.ob), 3)
head(showSol(scmp.ob), 3)
head(showGroupCoeff(scmp.ob), 3)
```

## The settings

`showParams()` lists every setting that the steps used, and the steps take
their defaults from them: `sc.t.fit()` uses the family, the link and the
level of `sc.p.vector()` unless told otherwise.

```{r params}
showParams(scmp.ob)
```

## Objects from earlier versions

The `version` slot records the version of scMaSigPro that created an object.
An object saved by an earlier version, with `saveRDS()` or `save()`, may
lack a slot or a setting that the current version needs; the steps then
stop and ask for `updateObject()`, which adds what is missing and says what
it changed:

```{r update-object, eval = FALSE}
scmp_ob <- updateObject(readRDS("analysis.rds"))
```

A current object is returned unchanged:

```{r update-current}
identical(updateObject(scmp.ob), scmp.ob)
validObject(scmp.ob)
```

# Equivalence with maSigPro

scMaSigPro fits the models of maSigPro [@conesa2006; @nueda2014] to
pseudo-bulk counts. Its design, tests, stepwise selection and gene lists are
implemented anew, without calling maSigPro, and with the settings of
maSigPro, without the offset, they give the same results. This part runs
both packages on the data of maSigPro and checks that every result is
identical. It runs when maSigPro is installed:

```{r masigpro-install, eval = FALSE}
BiocManager::install("maSigPro")
```

```{r no-masigpro, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
#| eval: !expr '!requireNamespace("maSigPro", quietly = TRUE)'
cat(
    "*maSigPro is not installed, so the code of this part is shown but",
    "not run.*\n"
)
```

## A Gaussian model on microarray data

`data.abiotic` holds the expression of 1000 genes in a time-course
microarray experiment on potato plants: a control and three abiotic
stresses (cold, heat and salt), at 3, 9 and 27 hours, with three replicates
each, 36 samples in all.
`edesign.abiotic` describes the samples with one 0/1 column per group;
scMaSigPro takes one column with the group instead.

```{r abiotic-data}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("maSigPro", quietly = TRUE)
library(maSigPro)
data("data.abiotic", "edesign.abiotic", package = "maSigPro")
head(edesign.abiotic, 3)

samples <- as.data.frame(edesign.abiotic)
groups <- c("Control", "Cold", "Heat", "Salt")
samples$Group <- groups[max.col(samples[, groups], ties.method = "first")]
samples <- samples[, c("Time", "Replicate", "Group")]
head(samples, 3)
```

Each sample is a bin of its own (`use_as_bin = TRUE`), so `sc.squeeze()` is
not needed. The design of `sc.set.poly()` is that of `make.design.matrix()`:

```{r abiotic-design}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("maSigPro", quietly = TRUE)
scmp_ab <- create_scmp(
    counts = as.matrix(data.abiotic),
    cell_data = samples,
    ptime_col = "Time",
    path_col = "Group",
    use_as_bin = TRUE
)
scmp_ab <- sc.set.poly(scmp_ab, poly_degree = 2)
design <- make.design.matrix(edesign.abiotic, degree = 2)

stopifnot(
    identical(predictors(scmp_ab), design$dis),
    all.equal(pathAssign(scmp_ab), as.matrix(design$edesign))
)
```

`sc.p.vector()` with the Gaussian family, the identity link and no offset is
`p.vector()`, and `sc.t.fit()` is `T.fit()`. maSigPro prints its progress;
`capture.output()` keeps it out of the vignette.

```{r abiotic-fit}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("maSigPro", quietly = TRUE)
invisible(capture.output(
    fit <- p.vector(data.abiotic, design,
        Q = 0.05, MT.adjust = "BH", min.obs = 20
    )
))
scmp_ab <- sc.p.vector(scmp_ab,
    family = gaussian(), link = "identity", offset = FALSE,
    min_na = 20, epsilon = 1e-5, max_it = 25, verbose = FALSE
)

invisible(capture.output(
    tstep <- T.fit(fit, step.method = "backward", alfa = 0.05)
))
scmp_ab <- sc.t.fit(scmp_ab, verbose = FALSE)

res <- scmpResults(scmp_ab)
fitted <- rownames(fit$p.vector)
stopifnot(
    identical(res[fitted, "p_value"], unname(fit$p.vector[, 1])),
    identical(res[fitted, "adj_p_value"], fit$p.adjusted),
    identical(rownames(res)[res$non_flat], rownames(fit$SELEC)),
    identical(showSol(scmp_ab), tstep$sol),
    identical(showCoeff(scmp_ab), tstep$coefficients),
    identical(showGroupCoeff(scmp_ab), tstep$group.coeffs),
    identical(as.data.frame(showTS(scmp_ab)), tstep$t.score)
)
sum(res$non_flat)
```

The gene lists of `sc.filter()` are those of `get.siggenes()`; maSigPro pads
its lists with blanks to the same length:

```{r abiotic-lists}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("maSigPro", quietly = TRUE)
sigs <- get.siggenes(tstep, rsq = 0.6, vars = "groups")
scmp_ab <- sc.filter(scmp_ab, rsq = 0.6, vars = "groups")
res <- scmpResults(scmp_ab)
for (list in colnames(sigs$summary)) {
    expected <- sigs$summary[[list]]
    expected <- expected[expected != " "]
    found <- rownames(res)[res[[paste0("sig_", list)]]]
    stopifnot(identical(found, expected))
}
colSums(as.data.frame(res[, grep("^sig_", colnames(res))]))
```

`plotTrend()` plays the part of `PlotGroups()` of maSigPro: the expression
of one gene in each group over time, with the fitted curve of each group.

```{r abiotic-plots, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("maSigPro", quietly = TRUE)
#| fig.alt: >
#|   Expression of the gene STMDE66 over time in the four groups of
#|   data.abiotic, with the fitted curve of each group, drawn by scMaSigPro.
plotTrend(scmp_ab, "STMDE66",
    logs = FALSE, pseudoCount = 0, summary_mode = "mean",
    significant = FALSE, lines = TRUE
)
```

## A negative binomial model on counts

`NBdata` holds counts of 100 genes simulated with a negative binomial
distribution, in two groups with six time points and three replicates
each; the first 20 genes change over time. With the negative binomial
family, theta 10 and no offset, `sc.p.vector()` and `sc.t.fit()` are
`p.vector(counts = TRUE)` and `T.fit()`:

```{r nb}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("maSigPro", quietly = TRUE)
data("NBdata", "NBdesign", package = "maSigPro")
samples <- as.data.frame(NBdesign)
samples$Group <- c("Group.1", "Group.2")[
    max.col(samples[, 3:4], ties.method = "first")
]
samples <- samples[, c("Time", "Replicates", "Group")]

nb_family <- MASS::negative.binomial(theta = 10)
design <- make.design.matrix(NBdesign, degree = 2)
invisible(capture.output(
    fit <- p.vector(NBdata, design,
        Q = 0.05, MT.adjust = "BH", min.obs = 6, counts = TRUE, theta = 10
    )
))
invisible(capture.output(
    tstep <- T.fit(fit,
        step.method = "backward", alfa = 0.05, family = nb_family,
        epsilon = 1e-5
    )
))

scmp_nb <- create_scmp(
    counts = as.matrix(NBdata),
    cell_data = samples,
    ptime_col = "Time",
    path_col = "Group",
    use_as_bin = TRUE
)
scmp_nb <- sc.set.poly(scmp_nb, poly_degree = 2)
scmp_nb <- sc.p.vector(scmp_nb,
    family = nb_family, offset = FALSE, min_na = 6, epsilon = 1e-5,
    max_it = 25, verbose = FALSE
)
scmp_nb <- sc.t.fit(scmp_nb, verbose = FALSE)

res <- scmpResults(scmp_nb)
stopifnot(
    identical(res$p_value, unname(fit$p.vector[, 1])),
    identical(res$adj_p_value, fit$p.adjusted),
    identical(rownames(res)[res$non_flat], rownames(fit$SELEC)),
    identical(showSol(scmp_nb), tstep$sol),
    identical(showCoeff(scmp_nb), tstep$coefficients)
)
sum(res$non_flat)
```

## What scMaSigPro adds

On single cells, scMaSigPro adds what the cells need before the model of
maSigPro applies [@srivastava2024]: the bins along pseudotime
(`sc.squeeze()`), the shared root (`sc.restruct()`), the size-factor offset
for the bins, the choice of the reference path, and the estimation of theta.
It also fits the genes in parallel with BiocParallel, offers the F test of
the full model, and returns the results as a `DataFrame` or in the
`rowData()` of the data. The
[Model and tuning](
    https://spriyansh.github.io/scMaSigPro/articles/model-and-tuning.html)
vignette describes these settings.
